claim: FAST-ONN (VCSEL + SLM free-space in-memory ONN) measured throughput of the current prototype
locator: Main text, Discussion, paragraph beginning "We experimentally achieved optical convolution"
quote: Currently the throughput T = 45 GOPS, limited by the low channel counts and clockspeed R = 100 MS s−1.
notes: Workload: 3x3 convolution kernels (5x5 VCSEL array, 3x3 fanout, 9 channels) at 100 MS/s; only the 2nd conv layer (2x2 kernels) of a ResNet-18-based COCO car-vs-background classifier ran optically, everything else digital. Precision 5-6 bit (Supp. Table S2). Not a transformer.

claim: FAST-ONN "full-system" energy for the current 9-channel 100 MS/s configuration is a component-level estimate using literature DAC/TIA/ADC/nonlinearity energies, not a measured wall-plug value
locator: Main text, Results subsection "Energy efficiency"; Supplementary Information Section III, Table S1
quote: With appropriate electronic circuitry, our FAST-ONN system can achieve an energy efficiency of about 370 fJ·OP−1 (~3 TOPS·W−1), which is similar to a state-of-the-art GPU.
notes: Table S1 breakdown per OP: VCSEL bias (electrical, measured ~400 uW/VCSEL) 220; DAC 25 (0.5 pJ/conv, literature); SLM 15 (3 uW/pixel prorated); TIA 10; ADC 44 (0.8 pJ/conv, literature); electronic nonlinearity 55 -> 369 fJ/OP. 1 MAC = 2 OP -> ~738 fJ/MAC. EXCLUDED: memory/weight loading, host/FPGA, thermal control, full SLM panel power (see R3-004). Handoff called this a "full-system prototype" number: it is an estimate "with appropriate electronic circuitry".

claim: FAST-ONN projected energy if scaled to 32x32 VCSELs x 32x32 fanout at 25 GS/s
locator: Main text, Results subsection "Energy efficiency"; Supplementary Table S1 "Near-term development" column (R=25 GS/s, N=M=1000)
quote: If the system scales to the 32 × 32 VCSELs with 32 × 32 fanouts, an efficiency of 2 fJ·OP−1 (500 TOP·W−1) might be reached (Supplementary Table S1)
notes: Projected breakdown (Table S1): laser 0.1, DAC 0.25, SLM 0.06, TIA 0.085, ADC 1 (2 pJ/conv), nonlinearity 0.5 fJ/OP. Assumes 5 mW/VCSEL at 25% wall-plug efficiency and 25 GHz clock (not demonstrated; prototype ran at 100 MS/s). ADC dominates at scale. Memory/host still excluded. Optical-core + converter number, not a system number.

claim: If the whole SLM panel power (8 W) is charged to the measured 45 GOPS instead of prorating 3 uW per used pixel, SLM weighting alone costs ~178 pJ/OP
locator: Supplementary Information Section III, footnote to Table S1
quote: The SLM consumes about 8 W (for external supply, the controller electronics, and the LCOS panel) for a total of 1920 × 1200 pixels, resulting in a power cost of about 3 μW per pixel.
notes: DERIVED: 8 W / 45e9 OP/s = 1.78e-10 J/OP. Shows how per-op numbers depend on prorating: the prototype uses a few hundred of 2.3M pixels. Not a paper claim.

claim: Programmable photonic unitary processor (8x8 silica PLC MZI mesh for fibre-mode MIMO descrambling, NOT an AI accelerator): 56.8 fJ/MAC for the "current prototype" is heater power / hypothetical 88-wavelength throughput
quote: Dividing each power estimate by this throughput gives about 56.8 fJ MAC−1 for our current prototype at 6.4 W, and ~9.6 fJ MAC−1 for the optimized MPLC three-stage case at 1.1 W.
notes: INCLUDES ONLY estimated static thermo-optic heater power (6.4 W = 0.1 N^2 W assuming mean phase excursion pi/2; not a measured wall-plug). EXCLUDES lasers, transmitters/modulators, coherent receivers, DACs/ADCs, DSP. Throughput is hypothetical (N=8, 10 GBd, 88 WDM channels = 1.1e14 MAC/s); experiment used 3-mode fibre and 12-GBd PDM-QPSK. Workload is optical-channel equalisation, not neural-network inference. Check: 6.4 W / 1.1264e14 = 56.8 fJ.

claim: Same paper: optimized three-stage MPLC with thermally isolated heaters
quote: Dividing each power estimate by this throughput gives about 56.8 fJ MAC−1 for our current prototype at 6.4 W, and ~9.6 fJ MAC−1 for the optimized MPLC three-stage case at 1.1 W.
notes: Heater-only, 1.1 W design estimate (Ppi 0.09 W trench-isolated heater, 3N heaters) / same hypothetical 1.1e14 MAC/s. Not built.

claim: Same paper: platform change to Si or SiN phase shifters (three-stage MPLC)
quote: By changing the silica platform to Si or SiN, the energy efficiency could be improved to ~1.9 fJ MAC−1 (Si) or ~3.0 fJ MAC−1 (SiN).
notes: From 0.216 W (Si, 0.018 W/pi) and 0.336 W (SiN, 0.028 W/pi) heater power / 1.1264e14 MAC/s (my check: 1.92 and 2.98 fJ). Heater-only; authors note higher propagation loss and polarization-diversity cost.

claim: Throughput basis used for all three fJ/MAC figures in source 28 is an assumed WDM configuration
quote: For N = 8, B = 10 GBd and M = 88 channels on a 50-GHz grid across the C band, the throughput is approximately 1.1 × 1014 MAC s−1.
notes: Counts 2N^2BM MAC/s. 88 simultaneous channels were not demonstrated in the transmission experiment.

claim: Thermo-optic phase shifters in the source-28 PLC prototype need about 0.2 W each for a pi shift
quote: All phase shifters in our PLC prototype are thermo-optic heaters, each requiring about Pπ = 0.2 W for a π shift
notes: Device parameter stated by authors. Static holding power dominates this class of device.

claim: C018 (passive transform): a fixed transformation realised passively would need zero holding power (discussion statement)
quote: the same transformation could be realized in a passive form, in which case the required power would be zero
notes: Applies ONLY to phase-shifter holding power for a transformation that never changes. Lasers, modulators, detectors, converters still draw power. Transformer weights are too large to hold in one static passive device; see R3-012 (reprogramming cost).

claim: C018 (self-holding PCM): phase-change elements draw energy only when reconfigured (discussion statement)
quote: self-holding phase-change elements, which require energy only during reconfiguration and exhibit essentially zero standby power
notes: Not measured in this paper. Reconfiguration energy per element is microjoules (R3-012) and endurance is finite (R3-013).

claim: Energy to reprogram one non-volatile Sb2Se3 PCM phase shifter (30 um, ITO heater, on SiN), one set + one reset pulse
quote: During the non-volatile switching cycles, the set pulse is 0.006 W/µm with a duration of 20 µs, and the reset pulse is 0.0035 W/µm with a duration of 600 µs.
notes: DERIVED: set 0.006 W/um x 30 um x 20 us = 3.6 uJ; reset 0.0035 W/um x 30 um x 600 us = 63 uJ. Preprint (not peer reviewed). This is the price of "zero standby power": at 67 uJ per rewrite, re-tiling a transformer weight matrix through PCM is far more expensive than holding it electronically unless each weight stays in place for very many uses.

claim: Endurance of Sb2Se3 non-volatile photonic phase shifters
quote: The Sb2 Se3 -based phase shifters exhibit robust and repeatable operation for up to 140 million switching cycles.
notes: Failure mode: ITO heater electrical breakdown. Preprint. Limits PCM weights to static or rarely-updated matrices.

claim: Capacitive electro-optic analog memory (DEOAM) on a microring leaks and needs refresh: retention time constant 0.835 ms
quote: Retention time from leakage is 0.835 ms for one time constant (τret) at 0.5 dBm optical bus power.
notes: Counter-example to C018: self-holding does not apply to capacitive analog memory. Leakage grows with incident optical power. The paper evaluates the network by emulation (MNIST 784-50-10), not a full hardware run. Its main claim: DACs drop from n^2 to n.

claim: Partial-coherence paper assumes PCM weighting elements draw no power for fixed kernels in its energy estimate
quote: The use of phase-change material as non-volatile photonic memory will consume no power as the weight matrix presents fixed kernels.
notes: Assumption only; weight-programming energy is not counted.

claim: "65 TOPS" optoelectronic multi-core OPU: the headline is per-wavelength throughput multiplied by 31 wavelengths and 4 cores
locator: Main text, Results section "WDM-based multi-task optical convolutional operation", paragraph on computational speed
quote: the total computational speed reaches 524.52 GOPS × 31 × 4 = 65.04 TOPS.
notes: Paper arithmetic: 18 ops/cycle/core x 29.14 GBaud = 524.52 GOPS per wavelength per core. Each core is a 1x9 weight vector (3x3 kernel). Convolution demonstrated with 24 (signed) / 31 (non-negative) wavelengths on core 1; the conclusion calls 65.04 TOPS "experimentally" demonstrated. Workload: image edge-detection convolutions and a MNIST OE-CNN (1 optical conv layer + electronic FC). Not a transformer.

claim: 65-TOPS OPU energy efficiency is a component-model estimate dominated by laser power (94%)
locator: Supplementary Note 8 "Energy efficiency" and Supplementary Table 1
quote: The total power consumption is therefore calculated to be 97.30 W according to Eq. (15). The maximum computing speed is calculated as 65.04 TOPS. Consequently, the efficiency is 1.50 pJ/OPS.
notes: Breakdown (Supp. Table 1): laser incl. SOA 91.54 W (94.08%; shot-noise/capacitance bound with a 47 dB link-loss factor), DAC 0.25 W (FoM-scaled 8.06 mW each), modulators 4.75 W (1 pJ/bit), ADC 0.70 W (FoM-scaled 5.66 mW each, 5-bit), heaters 0.06 W. Detectors "negligible". EXCLUDES DRAM, I/O, host. Not measured. = 3.0 pJ/MAC.

claim: Same OPU with realistic off-the-shelf ADC/DAC powers instead of FoM-scaled ones
quote: the overall system power consumption is estimated to be 123.76 W, corresponding to an energy efficiency of 1.90 pJ/OPS.
notes: ADC 199 mW each (10-bit 32 GS/s), DAC 88 mW each (8-bit 28 GS/s) -> ADCs 24.68 W, DACs 2.73 W.

claim: Source 30 excludes off-chip memory and system I/O from its "system-level" energy comparison
locator: Supplementary Note 13 "System-level compute density and energy efficiency"
quote: off-chip memory access (e.g., DRAM) and system-level I/O overhead are excluded for both optical and electronic implementations
notes: System-level figure 1.50x0.76 + 5x0.24 = 2.34 pJ/OP assumes ~5 pJ/OP for the electronic 24% of ops. Paper claims ~2.14x vs all-electronic under the same assumptions.

claim: Measured computational precision of the 65-TOPS OPU
locator: Supplementary Note 7 "Computational precision and improvement methods"
quote: yielding a final computational precision of 4.68 bits
notes: From std 0.0779 over 49,284 convolution results. MNIST OE-CNN accuracy 95.08% (best of 10 training runs; main text).

claim: Single-shot matrix-matrix diffraction processor (16x16-by-16x16): stated throughput at 2 GSa/s
quote: For the current parallel diffractive beam routing, N = M = 16, and C=2 Gsa/s, the system throughput is 2N2MC = 16.3 TOPS.
notes: Formula result. The full 16x16 MMM bit precision was characterised at 100 MSa/s (AWG-channel limited): 8.5 bits (ENOB 6.8). 2 GSa/s was verified on Mux/Demux subsets (~8 bits).

claim: Single-shot MMM processor "total system energy" is a nominal-component model that contains no laser term

quote: the total system energy consumption is 250 fJ/MAC, which corresponds to a computing efficiency of 8.1 TOPS/W
notes: Model (Supp. Table 2): data/weight modulators ~1 pJ each, DACs ~1 pJ, ADC ~1 pJ, photoreceiver/integrator ~1 fJ, nonlinearity <100 fJ -> (2/M + 2/N + 1/NT) pJ with N=M=16, T=100 = 0.25 pJ/MAC. Laser wall-plug, memory, host are NOT in the table. Nominal "~1 pJ" values are assumptions, not measurements.

claim: Single-shot MMM processor projected energy with segmented optical DACs
quote: decrease the system energy consumption to 5 fJ/MAC and increase the computing efficiency to over 600 TOPS/W.
notes: Relies on a 40 fJ/operation 8-bit optical DAC (cited) and the same laser-free accounting.

claim: Optical energy at the detector sufficient for high MAC precision (time-integrating receiver)

notes: Optical energy only, at the receiver; not laser wall-plug. Shows the physics floor is not the constraint.

claim: Accuracy vs digital baseline, single-shot MMM processor (CNN+FC on MNIST)
locator: Main text, Results, MNIST demonstration paragraph (Fig. 6b,c)
quote: we demonstrate 96.4% classification accuracy of our optical processor for 1000 MNIST images, which is close to the pre-trained (fully digital) accuracy of the network (97.5%).
notes: ReLU, normalisation and softmax done digitally.

claim: C014: SLiM single-layer photonic chip ran GPT-like language models experimentally (0.345B parameters, 384 layers) plus a 100-layer ImageNet CNN
locator: Abstract; Results (Fig. 5a); Methods "Deep neural network with SLiM chips"
quote: We experimentally constructed a neural network with 100 layers for image classification, along with a 0.345-billion-parameter LLM with 384 layers for text generation
notes: How it ran: all matrices decomposed into 8x8 elemental matrix cores (Methods), inputs on 8 ITU wavelengths, bench AWG (Keysight M8195A) + oscilloscope, 1-bit converters and sign activation; evaluated on 356 token samples. Token accuracy 43.92%, loss 3.04 (0.345B). Supp. Table S1: A100 digital loss 2.955 vs SLiM 3.0397 on same network. CONTRADICTION: Supp. note says K=128 "in the SLiM experiments of Fig. 4-5", Methods says 8x8 cores.

claim: SLiM "system efficiency" is a calculation for a 128x128 chip at 10 GHz with 1-bit converters and literature per-channel powers
locator: Supplementary Note (energy analysis), lines 243-274; Supplementary Table S1 footnote a (PDF prints review line numbers 271-274 inside this sentence; omitted from quote)
quote: the system efficiency reaches 856.85 TOPS/W while considering the power consumption of modulators, detectors, optical power sources, transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), Digital-to-Analog Converters (DACs), and Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs).
notes: Per-channel inputs: phase shifter 1.7 uW, DAC 63 uW (6.3 fJ/bit), laser/source 200 uW, 250 uW, TIA 2.2 mW, ADC 273 uW (27.3 fJ/bit comparator). EXCLUDES memory, weight loading, host, bench instruments actually used. My recomputation from the listed values: 0.410 W for 3.2768e14 OP/s = ~799 TOPS/W; 856.85 is only reproduced (~857) if the MN x phase-shifter term is dropped. Discrepancy flagged (PDF subscripts garbled).

MNIST CNN accuracy 92.4% vs 95.0% theoretical. Light source = 54% of the estimate.

claim: Incoherent LED/LCD multilayer optoelectronic network: estimated efficiency of the proof-of-concept at 800 kHz

claim: Laser wall-plug floor for a 1000-input single-pass crossbar at 10 GS/s, 5-bit at the detector, 20 dB optical loss, 40% wall-plug efficiency; ADC/DAC neglected
locator: Supplementary Note 1 "Optical Energy Overheads in Single-pass Architectures"

notes: Optical budget ~35 W for N=1000 (NEP_Ge 5e-12 W/rtHz). Scaling given: laser overhead = 10^(2 + 0.1 x PIC loss dB)/N fJ/MAC, i.e. 78 fJ/MAC at N=128. Higher precision raises this: 8-bit adds ~18 dB SNR. Main text of the perspective is paywalled.

notes: "Full system implementation with ADCs/DACs"; ABFP16 number format, 10-bit/7-bit DAC inputs, 11-bit ADC outputs, 500 MHz sustained (2 GHz peak). Host CPU, PCIe, DRAM outside the 78 W. claim: Lightmatter: ratio of full-system to photonic-core power

notes: Transformer ops sampled from a real LM were run on an SLM-based optical MVM; the rest is a calibrated simulation. Requires 1e4 x 1e4 optical MVMs every 0.1 ns (not built). Baseline is A100 at ~300 fJ/MAC, not B300. TMLR 2024 published version not re-checked.

claim: Optical Transformers: electronics, not optics, account for nearly all energy in an optical Transformer
quote: since the optical computation itself is so cheap the electronics account for nearly all of the energy cost
notes: Electrical costs = amplification + modulation + memory access + DAC/ADC.

claim: Attention (activation x activation products, KV cache) cannot use weights-in-place optics; both operands must be loaded and encoded each time
quote: For attention, weights-in-place is not possible, as the matrix products are between activation data.
notes: Structural reason photonics does not remove the decode memory wall: KV-cache reads remain an electronic memory cost.
